{"consolidated_memory":"**Intermittent EOF in crypto/tls/handshake.go - Five separate incidents (2026-01-20 to 2026-06-27)**

All incidents manifest the same problem: unexpected end of stream during TLS handshake negotiation in crypto/tls/handshake.go (security-side work). The common repro pattern is opening many short-lived connections in a row. Each occasion had a distinct trigger, root cause, and fix.

**Occasion 1: [2026-01-20] - OAuth provider sessions**
- Trigger: Sessions arriving through OAuth provider only
- Root cause: Missing Unicode normalisation before hashing
- Fix: Normalised to NFC ahead of digest (PR #3060, branch fix/intermittent-eof-1)
- Result: Flaky test went from 90 failures per hundred runs to zero

**Occasion 2: [2026-01-28] - Midnight boundary jobs**
- Trigger: Jobs scheduled across midnight boundary
- Root cause: Race in lazy initialisation
- Fix: Guarded init with double-checked lock (PR #5617, branch fix/intermittent-eof-2)
- Result: Memory settled at 803 MB instead of climbing past 3 GB

**Occasion 3: [2026-04-03] - After client retry**
- Trigger: Manifested after client had already retried once
- Root cause: Config loader reading wrong environment file
- Fix: Made environment selection explicit and failed closed on ambiguity (PR #5825, branch fix/intermittent-eof-3)
- Result: Alert stayed quiet for 74 consecutive days

**Occasion 4: [2026-06-01] - Large payloads**
- Trigger: Payloads above roughly 2 megabytes
- Root cause: Unbounded retry loop with no backoff
- Fix: Capped attempts and added exponential backoff with jitter (PR #7029, branch fix/intermittent-eof-4)
- Result: Job finished in 23 minutes instead of 4 hours

**Occasion 5: [2026-06-27] - Concurrent requests on same key**
- Trigger: Two requests racing on the same key
- Root cause: Listener registered but never removed
- Fix: Removed listener on teardown and asserted it in a test (PR #7062, branch fix/intermittent-eof-5)
- Result: p99 latency fell from 9.9 s to 867 ms

All fixes were applied to the same corner of crypto/tls/handshake.go with context carrying over between incidents."}
